messages:
ana: FYI customers hitting quota throttle during canary — root cause looks like provisional token rows decrementing per-route soft quotas immediately, even though many are later refunded. this causes customers to see spurious 429s.

harper: ouch. any example trace?

ana: here’s a short timeline from a single session:
```
2026-09-02T09:01:01Z router: session=s1 route=fast-us provisional=3 reason=prefix
2026-09-02T09:01:02Z router: session=s1 reconnect -> route=stable-us confirmed=40
2026-09-02T09:01:03Z ledger: provisional reduces fast-us soft_quota by 3
2026-09-02T09:01:04Z quota-enforcer: customer acct-88 hits soft_quota -> throttle 429
2026-09-02T09:01:05Z ledger: provisional marked probe and reconciled later -> refund issued
```

drew: so provisional rows are applied to quota immediately and the quota system treats them as committed. we need to separate provisional accounting from quota enforcement.

harper: or at least scope provisional decrement to a non-blocking soft reservation that doesn't trigger rate-limits. idea: provisional should reduce a "soft reserve" bucket and only affect hard enforcement when converted to confirmed.

ana: +1. we should also surface the soft-reserve usage in console so SREs and customers can see what portion of their quota is provisional. console-pm: can we add that tile?

console-pm: yes. propose: "quota breakdown" widget with three numbers: confirmed_used, provisional_reserved, available_hard. also a timeline showing provisional spikes vs confirmed drains. CON-999 opened.

billing-team: careful: if we stop provisional from counting toward user-visible quota, customers may open more concurrent streams and then get double capacity; we need clear semantics in docs and a short fallback: provisional reduces reserved_tokens but doesn't block quota until confirmed OR reserved exceeds safety_threshold. billing prefers a conservative approach: provisional contributes to a non-blocking reserve but we still enforce a conservative per-customer cap that includes a high-percentile projection of provisional-to-confirm conversion.

drew: implementable approach: (1) ledger marks provisional rows with tag "reserve" and a TTL 24h (2) quota-enforcer reads provisional sum but only enforces hard limit if confirmed + provisional > hard_limit OR projected_confirm_rate(provisional_group) > threshold (we can use recent historical conversion rate) (3) console surfaces both numbers and allows admin toggles for enforcement mode.

harper: need rollout safety: start with enforcement mode = conservative (provisional mostly non-blocking) behind FF, run 7-day shadow enforcement to identify customers who would have been blocked, and alert ops if any cross critical thresholds.

ana: also add a fast path for short probe-like sessions: if session UA matches probes and duration < 300ms, mark provisional as probe and exclude from projection used by enforcement. ops-bot: ticket CREATED QUOTA-432.

drew: QA plan: simulate mixed traffic with 20% probe recon, 10% legit retries, and bursty confirms. verify that with conservative enforcement customer-facing 429s drop by >90% while overall confirmed capacity remains within 1-2% of baseline.

billing-team: we'll need a CSV export of provisional cohorts and their projected confirmation rates for reconciliation and potential invoice adjustments. also manual refund workflow if misclassification found.

console-pm: UI note: add a tooltip explaining provisional semantics and an override button for customer success to temporarily lift conservative enforcement for specific tenants. track all overrides in audit logs.

ana: implementation tasks: INFRA-2011 quota change; LEDGER-725 tag provisional rows w/metadata; CON-999 dashboard; BILL-777 CSV/export & workflow. I'll start router patch to include origin metadata and a small quota-enforcer change.

harper: add unit tests for projected_confirm_rate logic and an e2e test sim for quota behavior.

ops-bot: created INFRA-2011, LEDGER-725, CON-999, BILL-777. closing thread, followups in tickets.
